sentences.text:
This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner questioning the action of respondents in not paying the full compensation in respect of the subject property of the petitioner namely Plot No.192 in Sy.No.286 in an extent of 36 x 36 feet which is equivalent to 144 square yards situated at Argul Village, Jakranpally Mandal, Nizamabad District and to declare the same as illegal and violation of the provisions The Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
2. Heard Sri V.Galaiah, learned counsel, representing Sri V.Mallik, learned counsel for the petitioner through video conference, Sri A.Kranthi Kumar Reddy, learned Standing Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent No.1 and the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition appearing on behalf of respondent No.3.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
No representation on behalf of respondent No.2.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as per the principles laid down by the Full Bench of the erstwhile High Court of Andhra Pradesh in Land Acquisition Officer-cum- Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella, Ranga Reddy District v. Mekala Pandu and others 1.

entities.text: Land Acquisition Officer-cum- Revenue Divisional Officer, Chevella, Ranga Reddy District v. Mekala Pandu and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In spite of repeated requests made by the petitioner, respondent Nos.2 and 3 authorities have not taken any steps to consider the same.

4. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for Land Acquisition submitted that the petitioner without approaching the respondent authorities and without submitting any representation/claim,
straight away approached this Court and filed the present writ petition.
She also submitted that if the petitioner submits representation/claim, respondent Nos.2 and 3 authorities will consider the same in accordance with law.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner by way of reply submitted that the petitioner may be permitted to submit the 1 AIR 2004 AP 250 detailed representation/claim before respondent Nos.2 and 3 authorities claiming compensation, as per the principles laid down in Land Acquisition Officer-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer (supra) and on such representation/claim, respondent Nos.2 and 3 authorities may be directed to consider the same and requested this Court to fix reasonable time.
6. Having considered the rival submissions made by the respective parties and after perusal of the material available on record, it reveals that the petitioner is claiming rights over the subject property, which was acquired for the purpose of National Highway.

1 authorities have not paid the full compensation.
7.

Taking into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case and in view of the submissions made by the respective parties, this Court deemed it appropriate to dispose of the writ petition granting liberty to the petitioner to submit representation/claim before respondent Nos.2 and 3 claiming compensation in respect of the subject property within four (4) weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this order.

On such representation/claim, respondent authorities are directed to consider the same and pass appropriate orders in accordance with law, within a period of eight (8)
weeks thereafter, duly taking into consideration the principles laid down in Land Acquisition Officer-cum-Revenue Divisional Officer (supra).
8.
With the above direction, the writ petition is disposed of.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
